title: Yachid, Echad, Kadmon: how the simple Essence holds every detail, like a nice guy's kindness
overview:
From chapter 10 to the end, the Mitteler Rebbe lays out the whole *hishtalshelus* in order, so that a person can trace anything in the world up to G-d and back down. But first one must contemplate its source, the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, and in detail. That sets up the chapter's paradox: *Yachid* means alone, with no parts, and yet the sources speak of ten *sefiros* there, even of a *Keser* and a *Malchus*. How can diversity come from simplicity?

The answer is the *hiyuli*. A nice guy's kindness is not a set of desires for coats and for shoes. It is one essence that includes every kindness he will ever be asked for, with its intellect, emotions, thought, speech and action, and none of them is there as a separate thing. So too a cat's power of movement, the soul's consciousness, and the light in the sun. From the *yechida* come three levels: the essence itself (*Yachid*), the power ready for a particular thing (*Echad*), and the deed fully estimated (*Kadmon*). Rabbi Walters calls chapters 10 to 13 the key to the whole book.

sections.title: From here to the end of the book: the four worlds in detail, and the Keser that unites each
sections.summary: The first nine chapters taught the method: trace a thing up the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent) to G-d and back down. Since not everyone knows the chain well enough, from chapter 10 the Mitteler Rebbe lays it out in order, down to the smallest subdivision, with the rule that the *Malchus* (kingship) of each level becomes the *Keser* (crown) of the next.

phrases.en: And now

phrases.he: הנה יש להבין דרך פרט בכל ד' עולמות דאבי''ע,
phrases.en: we have to understand the details of all of the four worlds of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*.

phrases.he: דהיינו בכל פרטי ענין עשר ספירות דאבי''ע
phrases.en: That means that we have to understand all the details of the ten *sefiros* of the worlds *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*:
their lights and their vessels,
how the lights go into the vessels, how the lights are enclothed in the vessels.

blocks.text:
"And now": now that the first part of the book, chapters one through nine, explained *hisbonenus* (contemplation) and how to do it. It should be done on the details of the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), or really, using the knowledge of those details, to look at the world and at particular things in it and see how they are connected all the way up and all the way down, until all the stages in the middle become transparent and you realize that you are looking at G-d.

That was the method of the first nine chapters, with some more details, but that is the basic idea: take something in the world and trace it all the way up, each stage of the *hishtalshelus* to its source, up to G-d Himself; see how it came from G-d; and then trace it back down, so that you recognize what you realized back in the physical world.

But as the Mitteler Rebbe pointed out at the beginning of chapter 5, not everybody knows the *hishtalshelus* well enough to do this. And it is difficult to piece together a working picture of it from learning scattered discourses, because they do not discuss the *hishtalshelus* in order. So the Mitteler Rebbe decided to make a book that explains the whole *hishtalshelus* in order, and that is this book, from chapter 10 to the end. Now that it was explained that you need to know the *hishtalshelus* in depth, he is going to explain it to you.

Now, at least for the benefit of those who do not know this yet, we have to understand the details of all four worlds, **Atzilus, Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya** (Emanation, Creation, Formation and Action). What are their details? All the details of the ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes) of each world, **their lights and their vessels**: the difference between the lights and the vessels, and also how the lights go into the vessels, how they are enclothed in them.

phrases.en: with all of their details:

phrases.he: גם בכל ספירה שמתחלקת לפרטי פרטיות
phrases.en: even how each *sefira* divides, subdivides into minute details, details after details, subdivision after subdivision.
Even, for example,

phrases.he: בבחינת חסד דמלכות שבחכמה שבמלכות דחסד
phrases.en: *chesed* of *Malchus* of *chachma* of *Malchus* of *chesed*,
and the like.

blocks.text:
**With all of their details**: what does that mean? Even how each *sefira* (one of the ten attributes) divides and subdivides, detail after detail, subdivision after subdivision.

"Even to the fifth degree, and really even more than the fifth degree; this is just an example." If you were told that we are now going to talk about **chesed of Malchus of chachma of Malchus of chesed** (*chachma* is wisdom), you should know what that is, and be able to explain it. Not just to know where it is on the map, but to really understand what it means.

Tell a person *chesed* (kindness) and he will say, "Oh, that means kindness." Once it goes to the second degree, *chesed* of *gevura* (might, restraint), most people already get confused. What is the difference between *chesed* of *gevura* and *gevura* of *chesed*? A lot of people do not know. So all these subdivisions will be explained later: how they work, and the different things we could mean when we say *chesed* of *gevura* or *chesed* of *Malchus*. **And the like.**

phrases.he: וענין יחודם והתכללותם בבחינת הכתר שבכל עולם,
phrases.en: We also need to understand how the ten *sefiros* of each world are united and included in the *Keser* of each world,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת הממוצע בין עולם העליון לתחתון הימנו
phrases.en: The *Keser* of each world is the intermediary between an upper and a lower world.

blocks.text:
We also need to understand how the ten *sefiros* of each world are united and included in its *Keser*. In the *Keser* of *Atzilus*, the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* all become one. And not only that: the *Keser* of *Atzilus* is really something greater than the ten *sefiros*, something that includes them all. That is the meaning of their *yichud* and *hiskalelus* (unity and inclusion): the *Keser* unites them, when the *Keser* is revealed it makes a unity among the *sefiros*, and when you have the *Keser* you have everything. All ten *sefiros* are included in the *Keser* of that world.

The same is true of *Beriya*: its *sefiros* are included in the *Keser* of *Beriya*. So the *sefiros* that come out in a world are really nothing new to its *Keser*. They are just its details, the *Keser* coming out in detailed ways and in vessels.

blocks.title: Ten garments, ten pools of water
blocks.text: This is what chapters 23 and 24 will explain: it is like one thing with ten garments, or like ten pools of water, where you pour into the first and it spills over into the next one, and the next one.

And the *Keser* of each world is **the intermediary between an upper and a lower world**. The *Keser* of *Beriya* is the intermediary between *Atzilus* and *Beriya*. The *Keser* of *Atzilus* is the intermediary between the *ma'atzil* (the one who emanates) and what is emanated, between *Atzilus* and what is higher than *Atzilus*, as will be explained later.

phrases.en: as is known, the general rule, the general principle, which in short summarizes the way that the *hishtalshelus* goes:

phrases.he: שמבחינת מלכות שבעליון נעשה כתר לתחתון,
phrases.en: that from *Malchus* of a higher level is made the *Keser* of a lower level,
and that is true all the way up to the highest levels.

blocks.text: There is a known general rule that sums up, in short, how the *hishtalshelus* goes: **from Malchus of a higher level is made the Keser of a lower level.** What that means and how it works will be explained. And it is **true all the way up to the highest levels**, which is why it is called a chain.

blocks.title: The links of a chain
blocks.text: *Hishtalshelus* means a chain. In a chain, the lowest part of the upper link connects with the highest part of the lower link and goes under it. In the same way, the *Malchus* of a higher level goes all the way down and actually goes a little lower than the *Keser* of the lower world. That is how it goes, all the way up and all the way down.

sections.title: The question: details, levels and sefiros in the simple Essence
sections.summary: Before the details of the chain, one must contemplate its source, the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* (the Essence of the infinite light) before the *tzimtzum* (contraction), and "even there" in detail: it has three levels, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon* (single, one and original), each with ten *sefiros*. But *Yachid* means alone, with no parts, so how can there be *sefiros* there, and how can diversity come from simplicity?

phrases.en: But first,

phrases.he: יש לכל מתבונן להתבונן במקור הראשון
phrases.en: it is first necessary for every person that's going to contemplate on G-dliness to contemplate on the first source where all of these things came from,
which is called the source of everything.

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: that is the essence of the infinite light
the way it is before the *tzimtzum* which is called the *makom panui*.

blocks.text: The first section was an introduction to everything that will be explained from here to the end of the book. Now the Mitteler Rebbe begins an introduction to this chapter, which explains the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* before the first *tzimtzum*.

Before he explains all the details of the *hishtalshelus*, how the worlds are created out of G-d's light, **every person that's going to contemplate on G-dliness** must first contemplate **the first source**, the *Mekora d'Kula* (the Source of everything).

Why is that necessary? Because we do not just want to learn how the world is created, "like this kabbalistic machine." The whole reason to learn the *hishtalshelus* is to see how it is really not there, how it is really G-d, a revelation of G-d. It only looks like a *hishtalshelus* because G-d made *tzimtzumim* and hid Himself like this and like that, "like He's pulling a trick on us." What we really want is to connect everything back to the first source: everything is here to be a revelation of G-d.

That first source is **the essence of the infinite light** as it is **before the tzimtzum which is called the makom panui** (the empty place). It is the *tzimtzum* that is called the *makom panui*, not the light. And it is not really the first *tzimtzum*, which is why he specifies "the one called the *makom panui*": there were *tzimtzumim* before it.

phrases.en: And even there, the essence of the infinite light before the *tzimtzum*, that also has to be understood in detail.
This is what is called elongating the *Echad*, dwelling on the *Echad*:
that you're supposed to dwell at length on G-d's simple unity.

blocks.text:
**And even there**: we said that the *hishtalshelus* has to be studied in depth, with all of its details, and this applies even to the essence of the infinite light before the *tzimtzum*: **that also has to be understood in detail.** "Which this is a question, already. Alarm should be going off in your head."

And this is not just some Chassidic trick. It is a thing *al pi nigleh* (according to the revealed law) that you are supposed to do.

This is what is called *ma'arich b'echad* (lengthening the word *Echad*), **dwelling on the Echad**. There is a halachic requirement, when you say *Shema* ("Hear, O Israel"), to lengthen the word *Echad*. But the way we rule, the main thing is not to say the word long. You can stretch it a little, but you are not supposed to stretch the letter *ches* too long, because then it is like adding an *alef*, and you are not supposed to say "*echade*", because that is not the word; the *dalet* is the end. So all you can do is say *Echad* and stress the *dalet*: you cannot really lengthen the word.

What you are supposed to do is say it, then pause and be *misbonen* (contemplate). It is a law that you stop and contemplate how G-d is one, the *alef* of *Echad*, over the seven heavens and the earth, the *ches*, which is eight, and the four corners of the world: that G-d is King over everything and controls everything. *Ma'arich b'echad* means to think about that at length, about all the details.

**That you're supposed to dwell at length on G-d's simple unity**: that itself seems to be a contradiction. How can you think in detail about G-d's unity, when seemingly there would be no details there? "It's just like a fact. That's it."

But *ma'arich* means to make it longer, the way a thing is explained *b'arichus* (at length), with a lot of explanations; otherwise it should not have said *ma'arich b'echad*. The belief every Jew has in G-d's unity, you should make long. As chapter 1 explains, that means you should explain it to yourself very simply, and you do that with a lot of explanations and a lot of *meshalim* (analogies). But seemingly, how can you, when it is a simple thing? That is what will be explained. This is still the introduction to the chapter, where he is only introducing ideas, and it is meant to set up this paradox in our mind; we are going to have this question for a while.

phrases.en: The simple unity is divided in general into three levels,
and each one of these three levels has ten *sefiros*.
These three levels are called *Yachid*, which means single, *Echad*, which means one, and *Kadmon*, which means original;

phrases.he: והכל בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and all of these three levels are all in the essence of the infinite light that precedes the first *tzimtzum* that we mentioned before.

blocks.text: So the *Atzmus Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, the simple unity, **is divided in general into three levels.** "What? It's divided into three levels? How does that make sense?" How can the simple unity be divided into three levels? We'll see. **And each one of these three levels has ten sefiros.** "So now we have thirty levels."

The three levels are **Yachid, which means single, Echad, which means one, and Kadmon, which means original**: an origin, the source of everything, the origin that must exist for everything after it to exist. And all three are in the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* that precedes the first *tzimtzum*. The first *tzimtzum* was mentioned a little in chapter 9, and what it is and how it works will be explained in chapters 12 and 13. Now he will start to explain these three levels, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, and then give *meshalim* for them.

phrases.en: *Yachid*, single, implies that it's alone.

phrases.he: והוא למעלה מהתאחדות נפרדים שנקרא אחד
phrases.en: So this is higher than the unity of parts, which is called *Echad*,
as is known.

blocks.text: What does *Yachid* imply? That it is alone. When you have a *ben yachid*, an only son, an only child, *yachid* means there is only one, a single. If you said *ben echad*, that would just mean one son, implying that there are more and you are speaking about one of them.

**So this is higher than the unity of parts, which is called Echad.** *Echad* comes from *achdus* (unity): different things that are united. In Hebrew *Echad* means two things: a one that has a two coming after it, and a one made up of parts, like a million or a thousand. *Yachid* means the only one, with no two and no three, and it means totally singular, with no parts, **as is known.**

blocks.title: One car
blocks.text: When you say you have one car, what do you mean? The car is a single unit, a single identity made up of many parts: the wheels and the chassis, the body, doors, an engine, a carburetor, a radiator, all kinds of things. Put it all together and you say you have one car. If you are missing part of it, it is not really a car; it is part of a car, a car missing this, a car missing that. And the fact that it can be divided into its parts shows that it is not a real entity, not its own thing. The car is not its own existence; it is just what you get when you put a bunch of other things together.

blocks.title: The computer
blocks.text: A computer is like that too. A computer is not really something new. Before they made computers they already had screens and monitors, typewriters, calculators and recording devices. The whole *chiddush* (novelty) of the computer is that they put them together. It is not really as if they made a new thing.

blocks.title: Pure olive oil
blocks.text: But *Yachid* means a pure thing, an elemental thing, not made up of something else. Like pure olive oil: it is only oil, there are no ingredients, and if you look at the label it says only "olive oil, 100% pure olive oil." Really, though, anything physical can be divided into parts. The olive oil is made of protein and carbohydrates and different kinds of molecules, and the molecules are made of atoms, and it divides into more parts. So physically there is nothing totally *yachid*. And spiritually too, the only thing that is *Yachid* is G-d; everything else is made up of parts, as is known. This is explained in other places, for example in *Chovos HaLevavos*.

phrases.en: So based on this,

phrases.he: בבחינת העצמות ממש לא יתכן לומר עדיין ענין עשר ספירות כלל
phrases.en: we cannot say that there's an idea of ten *sefiros* at all in G-d's essence, in the *Atzmus*.
like to say *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*;

phrases.he: שממילא מובן שקדם לזה בחינת כתר וחכמה כו'

blocks.text: **So based on this**, that *Yachid* is a higher unity than *Echad*, that *Yachid* means totally alone and *Echad* means made up of parts: G-d is perfect, He is in the manner of *Yachid*, there is just Him. So **we cannot say that there's an idea of ten sefiros at all in G-d's essence, in the Atzmus** (the Essence).

The *mashal* for *Malchus* is speech. If you see that somebody is talking, he must have had a *ratzon* (will) to talk, and a *sechel* (intellect) of how to talk and what to say, and all the other things, the *middos* (emotions): he must have felt like talking. When somebody is happy he feels like talking; when he is sad he does not. So he must have had all the *sefiros*.

So how can we speak of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite)? We cannot say there is anything of ten *sefiros* there, because G-d is totally singular: there is nothing besides Him and He is not made of parts. And yet we do say *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, and once we say it, there is a *Keser* of the *Ein Sof* and a *chachma* of the *Ein Sof*. "So this is the basic question." Sometimes it seems we say that there are *sefiros* even in the *Atzmus*, and other times we say that there are none there at all; and of course, how can you say there are *sefiros* there?

phrases.en: And the truth is,

phrases.he: גם בבחינת העצמות דאור אין סוף שנקרא לבדו
phrases.en: that even in the essence of the infinite light, which is called alone, the level of *Yachid*,
even there you can say that there are ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: אך שנקרא חכים לא בחכמה ידיעא
phrases.en: Only that we say that they are wise, and not with a knowable wisdom,
as is known,

phrases.he: עד ולאו מכל אלין מדות כלל.
phrases.en: really it has nothing to do with any of these *middos*.

blocks.text: **And the truth is** that even in the essence of the infinite light, **which is called alone, the level of Yachid**, where G-d is totally one with no parts, **even there you can say that there are ten sefiros.** How can you say that?

He is called wise, **and not with a knowable wisdom**: there is *chachma* there, but not a *chachma* you can know, not at all like your *chachma*, and really it has nothing to do with any of these *middos*. It is not like your *chachma* and not like your *bina* (understanding); G-d is beyond all these *middos*.

But seemingly, how does that answer the question? So the *sefiros* are there, only not as we know them. "But if they're there, it's still divisions, right?"

Remember why we are getting into this: we want to explain how the *hishtalshelus* and the ten *sefiros* really come from the *Atzmus Ein Sof*, simple, before the *tzimtzum*. So we have to understand how they are there. That is the basic question of this chapter: how can diversity come from simplicity?

What bothers us is that *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching), and not only *Chassidus*, the Torah, tells us that there is nothing except G-d, and that everything is really Him, revealing Himself in different ways and making it look like different things. Then we have a question: if there is really only G-d, and G-d is simple, how is it that I see all these different things? How is that revealing a simple G-d? The world and the *hishtalshelus* seem to be the opposite. This chapter comes to help us understand how they are revealing G-d, how the world and the *sefiros* and everything really come from Him.

sections.title: The answer in short: the light is as simple as the Essence, and the sefiros are there only as He estimated what would be
sections.summary: The light before the *tzimtzum* reveals the Essence exactly as it is, so it is as simple as the Essence: the *tehiru ila'a*, *Yachid*, one and not by the count of ten. We speak of *sefiros* there, a *Keser* and a *Malchus* even, only because of what He estimated in Himself would come about after the *tzimtzum*; the Essence is higher than them and yet includes them, like oil that floats above everything and permeates everything.

phrases.en: So what's the *inyan*?

phrases.he: דבאמת כמו שעצמות האין סוף הוא אור פשוט בתכלית הפשיטות,
phrases.en: that just like the essence of the *Ein Sof* is completely simple light,

phrases.he: כך ממש בחינת אורו וזיוו הנקרא אור אין סוף
phrases.en: so too, the light of the *Ein Sof* is also completely simple:

phrases.he: דהיינו הוא ושמו בלבד כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and this is what we said, that it's just G-d and His name alone.

blocks.text: So what is the *inyan* (the matter)? How is it that the *sefiros* are there? **Just like the essence of the Ein Sof is completely simple light, so too, the light of the Ein Sof is also completely simple.** The *Atzmus*, the *Ein Sof*, the *Maor* (the source of the light) is completely simple, and the light that comes out of it is also completely simple, because it is a revelation of the *Ein Sof* exactly the way it is. That is the idea of light: light reveals whatever you see the way it is. **It's just G-d and His name alone**, which is totally simple: Him, and He is totally simple, and His revelation of Himself to Himself, which is also totally simple.

phrases.en: And this is what is called the upper purity,

phrases.he: שזהו ענין ובחינת התגלות אור עצמותו כמו שהוא דוקא
phrases.en: that is the revelation of G-d's essence exactly the way He is.

blocks.text:
The *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum* is called **the upper purity**, the *tehiru ila'a*. Back to the pure olive oil: what does pure mean? That there are no parts, nothing else. The upper purity is when it is G-d and His name alone and there is nothing else at all. The lower purity, which will be discussed later, is after the *tzimtzum*: the whole world is seen as revealing Him, but already seen as something separate, only connected with Him. That is the lower level of purity.

What is the upper purity? **The revelation of G-d's essence exactly the way He is.**

phrases.en: And this is what's called *Yachid*, that it's alone,

phrases.he: שאין עוד מלבדו לומר בו לשון התאחדות
phrases.en: that there's nothing else, to say that there is an *achdus*, that there is a unification of parts,
*yichud* is like unite, that two things should unite.
This is what it says in *Pasach Eliyahu*, that You are one,
but not with a *cheshbon*, not with a calculation, not with a number.

blocks.text: **And this is what's called Yachid, that it's alone**: there is nothing else, so that you could say there is an *achdus* there, a unification of parts. *Achdus* means that things stay separate but work together. Like when you want *achdus* among the Jews: we stay separate people, we have our own ideas and sometimes we disagree, but nevertheless we all love each other and work together. *Yichud* means that you *mamash* (actually) become one thing, that you connect, like when a father and a mother have a child and become *mamash* one thing; even there it says *basar echad* (one flesh). *Yichud* means that two things unite. You cannot say either: there are no separate things there connecting or uniting, because it is just G-d.

This is what it says in *Pasach Eliyahu* (Elijah's opening prayer, in the *Tikkunei Zohar*): **You are one, but not with a cheshbon, not with a calculation, not with a number.** And the Arizal explains what *cheshbon* you might have made: a count of ten. You might have thought that G-d is one but made up of ten *sefiros*. No: He is one, not made up of ten *sefiros*, just G-d, totally simple. So the truth is that the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* is completely simple and has no ten *sefiros*, because it is a revelation of G-d exactly as He is, and that is called the upper purity.

phrases.en: But this that we said,
that G-d is wise, but not with a knowable wisdom, etc.,

phrases.he: שיש על כל פנים חלוקי מדריגות,
phrases.en: that implies that there are divisions, that there are still different levels:
there's wise and understanding and kind and compassionate.
When we speak of these divisions, we don't mean that from the side of G-d's *etzem* there are these divisions;

phrases.he: רק מצד מה ששיער בעצמו בכח מה שעתיד להיות בפועל אחר הצמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: rather, when we speak of the ten *sefiros*, we mean that since G-d decided to make a world, and in the world He decided to make ten *sefiros* and to make a division between these things, so we say that they came from Him.

blocks.text: So how do we say that there are ten *sefiros* there? We said they are there, only not as a knowable *chachma*. **But this that we said, that G-d is wise, but not with a knowable wisdom** implies **that there are divisions, that there are still different levels**: **wise and understanding and kind and compassionate**, and there is a difference between them. If there is a difference between calling G-d wise and calling Him understanding, between calling Him kind and calling Him merciful, there are already divisions of *sefiros* there. So it may not be a knowable wisdom, it may not be like my wisdom, "but who cares if it's like my wisdom?" If I can say this is different from that, that is already a division, even if it is much greater than my wisdom.

The answer is that "not knowable" does not mean just that it is not like our wisdom. It means, as he says, that it has nothing to do with these *middos* at all. You cannot even say that it is a *chachma*, or that there is a difference between *chachma* and *bina*: they are not definable at all. It is totally simple, just G-d, not a wisdom at all. So why do we say that they are there?
blocks.question: If the *sefiros* there are not a knowable wisdom, there is still wise and understanding, kind and compassionate: are those not divisions?

blocks.text: **When we speak of these divisions, we don't mean that from the side of G-d's etzem** (essence) **there are these divisions**, only from the side of what He estimated in Himself would be after the first *tzimtzum*. **Since G-d decided to make a world, and in the world He decided to make ten sefiros and to make a division between these things, so we say that they came from Him.** But we are not saying that, as they are in their source, they are separate things.

So it is like this. When we say the *sefiros* are not in the *Atzmus* of the *Ein Sof*, we mean that it is totally simple: G-d is so much higher than any *inyan* of *sefiros* that you cannot say there is a *chachma* there, because it is much higher than being *chachma*. You cannot say there is a *bina* there; at the level of the *etzem*, *chachma* and *bina* are the same thing. The real essence of the *chachma* is the same as the essence of the *bina*: it is really just G-d. "The whole *hishtalshelus* is an artificial thing, and really our job is to see that it doesn't exist."

We want to look past the *hishtalshelus* and see the *etzem*, see how it is really all one thing, just G-d. But to do that we have to go through all the details and see why they look different and how they look different, and then we will realize that they are not really different, and we will find the *etzem*.

blocks.title: Oil floats above and permeates
blocks.text: This is what is explained in different places, for instance in *Kuntres Inyana shel Toras HaChassidus*, in English "On the Essence of Chassidus": the *etzem* goes into everything but is really higher than everything, like oil. Oil floats above everything, and it also permeates everything. So the essence is higher than everything, higher than the idea of ten *sefiros*, and yet it can go into everything, into all the ideas of the *sefiros*.

blocks.title: An idea too deep to grab with your hand
blocks.text: When we say that there are not ten *sefiros* there, we mean that G-d is higher than everything, higher than wisdom or intellect or anything. As it says in *Tanya*, to say that G-d is so great that you cannot understand Him is like saying that an idea is so deep that you cannot grab it with your hand. "It's like a joke."

On the other hand, we say the *sefiros* are there, for two reasons. First, when we say that wisdom is not there, we do not mean, *chas v'shalom* (G-d forbid), that G-d is stupid, that He is missing something, missing *chachma*, that He cannot have wisdom. We mean that it is so much higher than wisdom that you cannot call it wisdom. And when we say that they are there, we are saying that G-d could come into wisdom, that G-d's existence includes wisdom: a much greater, higher existence, which includes the thing of wisdom too. Because He is G-d, He automatically has wisdom. That is what the Rambam says: the first thing is to realize that there is a first Being, higher than everything, and from Him comes everything; everything is just coming out of His existence, His being.

Wisdom is just coming out of G-d's existence, and a *mashal* will be given for how this works. The basic idea is that since we see wisdom in the world, it must have come from somewhere, and it could not have come from anywhere but G-d. So on the one hand we must say that G-d has wisdom, because it came from Him. On the other hand, the way it is in G-d is not like the way we know wisdom; not only is it unlike the wisdom we know, you cannot even call it a wisdom. It is a much higher thing, and at that level there is no difference between wisdom and understanding or anything; it is a much higher thing that connects everything.

That is what this chapter will explain: when you have a higher essence, it automatically includes all the parts, but to it they are all the same. That is the meaning of "like oil": it floats above everything, higher than any of the things, and yet it can go into everything, because to it they are all the same. G-d's essence is higher than anything and everything, and in that way it is unknowable. On the other hand it is found in everything, and a piece of the essence is the whole essence. You can find G-d's whole *etzem* in *chachma* and in *bina*, and all the way down in things in the world, a piece of cake or a tree: G-d's whole *etzem* is there.

In a way the whole rest of the book comes to explain this chapter, this point, because what the whole book is trying to help us do is look at everything in the *hishtalshelus*, everything in the world, in a two-step process. First, separate out the oil: find the essence, and realize that G-d is really higher than that thing, that the thing is not G-d, that there is a higher reality. Once we recognize that higher reality, reconnect it to the thing and see that the real essence of the thing is G-d; it is not really what we thought it was.

Take *chachma*. First we realize that *chachma* is not the ultimate thing: G-d is not wisdom, and G-d is not love; G-d is higher than that. Then we realize that what wisdom really is, is a revelation of G-d. It is higher than what we think wisdom is; it is a G-dly thing. And now we see everything as a G-dly thing. What this means will become clear as we start to do it throughout the book.

At the beginning of chapter 12 and at the end of chapter 13, where he explains the *tzimtzum*, he says that this is the whole point of man and the whole point of learning this book: basically these chapters, 10, 11, 12 and 13. In 10 and 11, to understand how the essence is higher than everything and yet everything is a revelation of it. In 12 and 13, to understand the *tzimtzum*, how it comes to look like something separate from G-d and is still really Him. The rest of the book is just the details of these chapters. "These four chapters is like the key."

So that is the basic point. G-d is really higher than all these divisions, the three levels of *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, the ten *sefiros*, everything. But since after the *tzimtzum*, in the *hishtalshelus*, He is revealed in divisions, in different levels and different *sefiros*, we say that they all came from before the *tzimtzum*. We do not actually mean to define levels before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקדש מלך בלשון האריז''ל עצמו ומבואר במקום אחר באריכות)

blocks.question: "Wait a minute, it says you're not allowed to talk about before the *tzimtzum*."
blocks.text: "This is really not a new thing that I'm telling you." The Mitteler Rebbe is saying that we can speak about before the *tzimtzum* like this. You are going to say to me, "Wait a minute, but it says you're not allowed to talk about before the *tzimtzum*." Where does it say that? In the writings of the Arizal: from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* and up you cannot speak about it.

But even the Arizal himself spoke about it. *Mikdash Melech* was written by one of the Arizal's students, "Rabbi Yisrael Saruk, I think was his name." He wrote down a *shiur* (class) of the Arizal, made a *hanacha* (a written record of it), and based on it wrote a book called *Mikdash Melech*. That book has the classes the Arizal gave on before the *tzimtzum*, which are not explained so much explicitly in Rabbi Chaim Vital's writings of the Arizal. That is why whatever we say about before the *tzimtzum* is usually quoted from *Mikdash Melech*. So there we see that the Arizal himself spoke about before the *tzimtzum* too.

And if you look there at the way it is explained, it is the same as what we are saying now. When we say you cannot speak about before the *tzimtzum*, we mean that you cannot say there are *mamash* different levels there, that there is *mamash* a certain *chachma* or *bina* there. But to say, as we are saying, that it is really higher than that, and that these things came from there, that you can say. So this has a source in Kabbalah too.

phrases.he: וזהו ענין כללות המאמר הראשון בזוהר,
phrases.en: And this is also the intention of the very first sentence of the *Zohar*:

phrases.he: בריש הורמנא דמלכא גליף גליפו בטהירו עילאה
phrases.en: in the beginning of the sovereignty of the king, he engraved an engraving in the upper purity.

phrases.he: פירוש בעצמות גלוי אורו הפשוט הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: That in the essence of G-d's simple revelation of light that we mentioned before,
which is called the upper purity,
he engraved an engraving:
that's the idea of engraving letters.

blocks.text:
**And this is also the intention of the very first sentence of the Zohar**, at least in some editions; in some editions it comes a little later. It translates "*Bereishis bara Elokim es hashamayim v'es ha'aretz*." How does it translate *Bereishis*, in the beginning? *B'reish hormanusa d'malka glif glifu b'tehiru ila'a*: **in the beginning of the sovereignty of the king, he engraved an engraving in the upper purity.**

*Hormanusa*, by the way, can mean two things: kingship, sovereignty, and also *ratzon* (desire): in the beginning of the king's desire. "Just keep both in mind, because here he's kind of saying both."

What does that mean? **In the essence of G-d's simple revelation of light that we mentioned before**, the revelation of G-d exactly as He is to Himself, **which is called the upper purity, he engraved an engraving.** What is engraving an engraving? **The idea of engraving letters.** *Glif glifu*: like the English glyph, as in hieroglyphic, which means letters.

phrases.en: And what does it mean, the beginning of the sovereignty, or the beginning of the *ratzon*, the beginning of his desire?
That means when it came up in his simple will to be king:
the beginning of the desire is the *Keser*, is the crown,

phrases.he: ובחינת האותיות שחקק הוא בחינת המלכות דאור אין סוף
phrases.en: and the letters that he engraved is the *Malchus* of the infinite light.

phrases.he: ואם כן יש ראש וסוף, כתר ומלכות,
phrases.en: That means that there's a beginning and an end, a *Keser* and a *Malchus*,

phrases.he: גם בבחינת עצמיות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: even in the essence of the infinite light.

blocks.text: **The beginning of the sovereignty, or the beginning of the ratzon, the beginning of his desire**, means **when it came up in his simple will to be king.** That beginning of the desire is the *Keser*, the crown, **and the letters that he engraved is the Malchus of the infinite light.**

**That means that there's a beginning and an end, a Keser and a Malchus, even in the essence of the infinite light.** Seemingly we are saying that there is already a *Keser* and a *Malchus* there, and so, in the middle, a *chachma* and a *bina*, a *chesed* and a *gevura*. So seemingly the first *maamar* of the *Zohar* already says that there are ten *sefiros* in the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*.

He is explaining that what we explained is the explanation of this first *maamar* of the *Zohar* too. We already asked the question and answered it, and now he is saying that this is also the meaning of the *Zohar*'s first *maamar*: a source for the idea, as is the explanation we find in the Arizal's *Mikdash Melech*.

phrases.en: The explanation is
that it came up in G-d's simple thought and desire:
that I am going to be king,
but everything is still within Himself.

phrases.he: קודם ענין מה ששיער בעצמו בכח דוקא כל מה שיהיה לו רצון למלוכה בגלוי,
phrases.en: This is still before he had a *hashara* of how he's going to actually want to be king; in other words, how it's going to be revealed after the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: והוא אחר הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי כו'
phrases.en: The actual revelation of kingship is after the *tzimtzum* that's called the *makom panui*.

blocks.text: What does it mean? **It came up in G-d's simple thought and desire** *Ana Emloch*, **that I am going to be king, but everything is still within Himself.** This is still before He had a *hashara* (an estimation) of how He would actually want to be King, how it would be revealed after the *tzimtzum*: **the actual revelation of kingship is after the tzimtzum that's called the makom panui.**

So this *maamar* of the *Zohar* is saying that in the level of *Yachid*, in the *Atzmus*, in the *Or Ein Sof*, there is an *inyan* of a *Keser* and of a *Malchus* before the *hashara*, before He estimated in Himself what He would do, how it would come after the *tzimtzum*. But the explanation is as we said: we are not saying that the levels are actually there. Once He estimated how to make the *hishtalshelus*, and decided to make ten *sefiros* in this whole way, we say that even before He decided it, before He estimated it, He already had the *yecholes* for it, the ability for it.

So this whole thing until now is an introduction to what this chapter will explain: the idea of a *hiyuli* (raw potential), "that's what we're going to call it", the kind of relationship where the essence is higher than everything and includes everything. He brought sources from Kabbalah that seem to say there are ten *sefiros*, while in other places we know it says there are not, and it seems a contradiction. He explained that really it is higher than the ten *sefiros*, but since they come out from there, we say they came from there and it is not missing them. Only the way they are there is not the way they come out: there it is really higher than being ten *sefiros*.

"Now, at this point, this is just like a bunch of words, and it doesn't necessarily make so much sense to us yet." So now the Mitteler Rebbe is going to give *meshalim* to understand it, as he always does: first he explains the idea briefly, with its sources in Kabbalah, and then he gives *meshalim* for it.

sections.title: The mashal: a nice guy's hiyuli desire for kindness
sections.summary: The powers of the soul, from will to action, are all hidden in the essence of the soul, the *yechida*. A kind person's *chafetz chesed* (desire for kindness) is a *hiyuli*, an essential power higher than any particular act, which includes every kindness he will ever be asked for, with all its intellect, emotions, thought, speech and action, totally united, until a situation draws one particular kindness out of it.

phrases.en: The likeness for this

phrases.he: ידוע מכחות הנפש בהתגלות מרצון עד המעשה
phrases.en: we can know from the powers of the soul, the way that they are revealed from the desire all the way until action:
that all of these soul powers, all of these different abilities and faculties and desires, all exist in detail, each one, every single one of them, not even one is missing,

phrases.he: בהעלם אור עצמות הנפש שנקרא בחינת יחידה
phrases.en: in the hidden light of the essence of the soul which is called *yechida*.

blocks.text: Now he is going to give some "analogies and metaphors and allegories and examples." **The likeness for this**, for the *Yachid* that is higher than everything, higher than ten *sefiros*, and yet has ten *sefiros* in it, **we can know from the powers of the soul, the way that they are revealed from the desire all the way until action.** There is a whole little *hishtalshelus*, a whole process, when you are doing something. First you want to do it, then you think about how to do it, then you talk to yourself or to other people about how to do it, and then you actually do it. You have emotions about it and intellect about it. It is a whole process: ten powers.

All these soul powers, all the different abilities and faculties and desires, **all exist in detail, each one, every single one of them, not even one is missing**, **in the hidden light of the essence of the soul which is called yechida.** Hidden in who you are, in the essence of your soul, are already all these different desires and abilities. Like what?

phrases.en: Like for example,

phrases.he: כאשר האדם הוא חפץ חסד וטוב להטיב בדבר פרט,
phrases.en: if a person is a nice guy, and they want to do a nice thing, they have a desire to do a nice thing,

phrases.he: שזהו בא מצד שיש בו מדה זאת דחפץ חסד וטוב בבחינת עצמות נפשו, הנקרא יחידה
phrases.en: because he has this *midda*, this character trait of kindness, in the essence of his soul, which is called *yechida*.

phrases.he: על כן בא חפץ חסד זה בגלוי מן העלמו
phrases.en: And therefore, because he's a nice guy, this desire for kindness became revealed in this situation.

blocks.title: Hot cocoa, fuzzy slippers and a knock at the door
blocks.text: **If a person is a nice guy**, he wants to help somebody. It is a cold winter day, it is snowing, and he is sitting there drinking his hot cocoa with a marshmallow in it and reading the paper. Then there is a knock at the door. He puts down his paper, gets up in his fuzzy slippers, goes over and opens the door, and there is the howling wind, snow blowing into the house, and a guy shivering in tattered clothes. He brings the guy in, gives him hot cocoa and wraps him up in blankets near the fire. When the guy thaws out a little, he asks him what he can do for him. "Oh, please, kind sir, I need a coat. It's freezing and I don't have a coat." So he goes into his closet, gives him a warm, fluffy down coat and some money to buy food, and sends him off. "That's the story that happened."

He did this nice thing **because he has this midda, this character trait of kindness, in the essence of his soul, which is called yechida**, the name of the highest level of the soul. If somebody asks you why he did it, you will say, "Because he's a nice guy. He's a nice person. He likes to help people."

**And therefore, because he's a nice guy, this desire for kindness became revealed in this situation.** If he were a mean guy, he would have slammed the door in his face: "Get a job! Don't bother me!" Or called security on him: "This guy's coming by bothering me." But he isn't; he's a nice guy. So he did this.

phrases.en: We must say,
with certainty,
that this desire for kindness, the way that it's included in the essence of his soul,
is in a way that is called a *hiyuli* power in his self,

phrases.he: לכלול כל מה שעתיד לחפוץ בחסד וטוב
phrases.en: and it includes everything that he is ever going to desire in goodness and kindness,

phrases.he: בכל פרטי פרטי הענינים שיבקשו ממנו
phrases.en: with all the little, little detail things that are going to be asked from him.

blocks.text: **We must say, with certainty, that this desire for kindness, the way that it's included in the essence of his soul, is in a way that is called a hiyuli power in his self.** What is a *hiyuli* power? An essence: totally simple, higher than any particular form, and therefore able to come into any form, to come out in anything.

It is an essential power within him, **and it includes everything that he is ever going to desire in goodness and kindness, with all the little, little detail things that are going to be asked from him.** Any little favor anyone will ever ask of him is included in the fact that he has kindness. We cannot say that he has a particular desire, a particular power or a particular kindness for each thing that will be asked of him. It is not like that.

blocks.title: The two beggars on the park bench
blocks.text: He does not have one desire to give this guy a coat and another for something else. The rest of the story is that the next day the guy he gave the coat to is sitting on a park bench next to his friend, and the friend says, "You know, I really need shoes," and shows him his shoes, all flappy, the sole coming off, holes in them, snow getting in. "Oh, why don't you go to this guy? Look, he gave me this coat." "Well, I don't need a coat." "Yeah, but he'll give you shoes." "How do you know he'll give me shoes?" "Because he gave me a coat." "I already told you, I don't need a coat. I need shoes." "No, but he didn't give me a coat because he has a kindness for coats." "Well, then how did he give you a coat?" "No, no, it's not that he doesn't have a kindness for coats, that he can't give coats. His kindness isn't for anything." "Well, then I definitely don't need him."

blocks.title: His kindness isn't for anything
blocks.text:
"No, no, it's not that his kindness isn't for anything, that it can't come for anything. It means that it's higher than anything; it's called a *hiyuli*. His kindness is just for whatever will be kind. He knows what kindness is, and whatever will be kind, he'll want it. It doesn't matter whether it's a shoe or a coat; it's all the same. If in this situation it will be kind, it doesn't matter what it is. It'll come into anything."

The desire for kindness will come into anything, even into things you do not normally think of as kind. If he is a surgeon, it will come into cutting people up, "because sometimes that's kind." He just knows what kindness is, and it will come out into whatever it fits. So we must say it is an essence that includes all the details that will ever be asked of him, but not that they are *mamash* there.

phrases.en: If so,
we must say

phrases.he: שקודם שעלה ברצונו וחפצו זה שבגלוי, להטיב חסדו בדבר זה הפרטי,
phrases.en: that before he had a desire to help this person in this particular way, to give him a coat,

phrases.he: היה כלול בעצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי
phrases.en: this desire was already included in the essence of his *hiyuli* power of kindness, in his essential power of kindness within himself.
And then, when the situation arises that the person needs the coat, it goes out from the essence,
and now it becomes revealed in this situation by being kind in that way.

blocks.text: **If so, we must say that before he had a desire to help this person in this particular way, to give him a coat, this desire was already included in the essence of his hiyuli power of kindness**, his essential power of kindness within himself. That is part of the identity of kindness: if you are a nice person, in such a situation that is what you will do. It is already included there.

**And then, when the situation arises that the person needs the coat, it goes out from the essence.** Now it is not just that he wants kindness and is a nice person: it becomes revealed in this situation by being kind in that way. In this situation the essence of kindness is expressed by giving him a coat. In a different situation it would be mean to give him a coat; in this one, if you are kind, you have to give him a coat. That is what a kind person will do. So we see that if a person really has kindness, it is an essence that includes everything, and he will want to do any and every kind thing that will ever come up.

And if he is missing even one *prat* (detail), it is not a real kindness. If it is missing the smallest thing, "it's not kindness, it's an organization. A foundation." They have these foundations that give out coats, but it is not a real kindness, because there is no person there with a desire to be kind. It is just a system: they give out coats, and if a person comes who needs a shoe, they say, "Sorry, we don't give shoes." Maybe one of the workers would be nice and give him money, but as far as the foundation goes, that is not what they do. You have to go to the next block; a person could die of starvation on the doorstep and they cannot help him, because that is not what they do. It was started by a kind person, and it could be helping and doing good, but it itself is a machine. It does not have the essence of kindness. If there were a real kindness there, it would come out in whatever would be kind: if a person needs food, you give him food too.

sensitivity.reason: A sharp generalisation about charitable foundations as machines that let a person starve on the doorstep.
sensitivity.publishable: If it is missing even the smallest detail, it is not kindness; it is a system. A system that gives out coats tells a person who needs shoes, "Sorry, we don't give shoes." One of the workers may be nice and help him, and the system may be doing good, but it itself has no essence of kindness, because there is no person there with a desire to be kind. If there were a real kindness there, it would come out in whatever would be kind: if a person needs food, you give him food too.

blocks.text: If a person says, "Okay, I'm a kind person and I'll do everything for you, but I won't give you shoes; if someone comes who needs shoes, I won't do that," that is not kindness. If it is missing even one thing, what do you mean? If you really want to be nice, if you really care, then whatever the person needs, you will want to do. As far as the desire to be kind goes, the person will want to do anything. You may say that maybe he has some thing about shoes, but that is a separate thing: as far as the kindness, he would want to do it, and maybe some other reason stops him. If he has a thing of kindness, he will want to do whatever the person needs.

So on the one hand, the kindness includes everything, and it must include every little detail: not just that it does, but it must, or else it is not kindness. And yet the details are not *mamash* there. There is no desire for a coat and a desire for shoes there; it is just kindness.

phrases.en: And we see

phrases.he: שיש בחפץ חסד זה שכל וחכמה ומדות ומחשבה ודבור ומעשה
phrases.en: that when this desire for kindness is revealed, when he actually wants to do something nice, there's an intellect, and there's a wisdom, and there are emotions, and there's thought, speech, and action.

blocks.text: **And we see that when this desire for kindness is revealed**, when he actually wants to do something nice, **there's an intellect, and there's a wisdom, and there are emotions, and there's thought, speech, and action.** It is a whole process. He has to evaluate the situation and figure out what will be kind in it.

You have to have a head, a *bissel sechel* (a little intellect). To be a nice person you can sometimes mean well, but if you have a strong desire to really be kind, you will also have to develop a certain amount of smarts, because otherwise you will try to help and sometimes do more harm than help. Part of the desire for kindness is to want to be smart about being kind.

There is also a kind way of understanding things: you look for the good, for ways to find merit and help for a person, as opposed to someone mean, who looks for fault and for reasons to hurt and punish. It is a certain perspective, a certain worldview, a kind *sechel*. And there is a wisdom, a certain creativity: being able to come up with creative solutions to people's problems, how to help them. You need a *chachma*, you need creativity.

Then there are the emotions. You have to feel for the person, be motivated, and included in that is a fear and a hate for whatever will oppose the kindness. If you want to help poor people who are starving, that gives you a hate for hunger and for what causes it, and a fear of them. You are passionate about it in a positive way and in a negative way. You will overcome any obstacles, which is *netzach* (victory); you will glorify kindness and how good it is, which is like *tiferes* (beauty), showing off how great an act it is; and you will laud the people who do it and give them prizes and honor, so that people want to do it. There is a whole way a kind person feels toward things, toward everything in the world. That is the emotions.

Your emotions are the way you relate to things, and your priorities and goals determine how you will relate to everything in the world. So there is a certain way you will have emotions if you are for kindness. And then of course you have to have thought, speech and action. You have to think about what you are going to do, and talk to people, or to the poor person: tell him, "Please come in," and ask him what size he is if you are going to give him a coat. And the main thing is the *maaseh* (action): you have to actually do it, actually give him the coat.

phrases.en: If so,

phrases.he: ודאי במקור חפץ חסד זה בהעלמו, כשהיה כלול בעצמיות החפץ חסד ההיולי, גם כן מהתחלקות שכל ומדות ומחשבה דבור ומעשה שבו
phrases.en: so we must say that included in the identity of kindness, his essential kindness, is already: if you know what it means to be kind, you already know how to think kind, how to feel kind, how to speak kind, how to do kind; you know how to do everything.

phrases.he: אבל בבחינת עצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי, כמו שהוא קודם שבא עדיין בדבר פרטי,
phrases.en: nevertheless, the way that these things are in the self of the essential kindness, before it comes to a particular thing,

phrases.he: הגם שבודאי גם שם יש התחלקות שכל ומדות כו',
phrases.en: even though even at that stage we must say that it includes intellect and emotions,
nevertheless, all these details, even though we must say that they're there, they're totally unified and they're included.

blocks.text: **If so**: when the desire for kindness is revealed, it comes out in all these different things. So we must say that included in the identity of kindness, in his essential kindness, is already all of it. If you know what it means to be kind, you already know how to think kind, how to feel kind, how to speak kind, how to do kind; you know how to do everything. The fact that he is a nice person means that he automatically knows how to have the *sechel* and the *middos*, intellect and emotions: it is all included there.

But **nevertheless, the way that these things are in the self of the essential kindness**, in what essential kindness is, **before it comes to a particular thing**, before it became a desire to give a coat, when it is just that you are a kind person: **even though even at that stage we must say that it includes intellect and emotions**. If you are a nice person, you must also have an intellect of kindness and emotions of kindness. You cannot just have a desire to be kind without these other things that go together with it. Kindness has to come into everything, or else it is not a real kindness: into the way he understands things, the way he feels toward things, and the way he thinks and speaks and acts.

There is a thing in Jewish law: if a person gives a lot of *tzedaka* (charity), a lot of money, but does it with a sour face, reluctantly, and makes the person getting it feel "like dirt", it is not as great a thing. It is much worse than giving a little with kind words, reassuring the person and making him feel good. Because one of the main things of kindness is not the act of giving money, making a donation. It is a whole attitude: that you care about the person, and you do not feel superior to him, as if you were doing him a favor. On the contrary, you feel that he is doing you a favor.

That is why it is called *tzedaka* in Hebrew, which means righteousness: you are just doing what is right. You feel that nobody deserves to go hungry, and that the fact that you have enough food for two people means that, because of the way the economy worked out, you ended up with this guy's share too, and it is only right to give him some. And especially from the Torah's point of view: the whole reason G-d made some people rich and some poor is so you can do the *mitzva* (commandment) of giving *tzedaka*. So really you owe him double: you can only do the *mitzva* because of him, and he has to suffer so you can do a *mitzva*, so "you really owe him big time." And the wheel of fortune turns; you could be in his shoes. There is no reason you should feel superior.

That is the whole attitude of really being kind. You cannot just act like it, or even try to talk in a kind way, if you do not sincerely feel that way, which only comes from this kind of understanding: of your relationship to the person, to your money, to your success. If that is not really your worldview, the kindness will not come out right. You will not really feel like helping the person; you will feel it is a bother and resent having to give away your money, and it can come out in all kinds of bad ways, which sometimes will lead to not kindness. So we must say that being kind already includes all those details, because if it does not come out in all of them, it is not really kindness.

**Nevertheless, all these details, even though we must say that they're there, they're totally unified and they're included.** By the fact that he is kind, it is automatically included that he has all those details. You do not need to say the details, and the details do not have their own existence; they are not a bunch of separate things that he has to have. "If you have kindness, you have everything." If you know what it means to be kind and you really want to be kind, you automatically know how to do all these other things, and you will want to do them.

sections.title: Every attribute is a hiyuli, and all ten are simply the self
sections.summary: Justice, beauty, victory and kingship are each a *hiyuli* like kindness, holding all their details united, as Napoleon's will to rule was in him as a baby. And the ten essential attributes themselves are not ten things united in the *yechida*: they are not separate from the essence at all. There is just you, the human essence, expressed in different arenas.

phrases.en: And the same way with a different character trait
within yourself,
like the attribute of *gevura*, which is, let's say, severity, or justice,
and the same thing with beauty, or showing off,
and the same thing with winning, with victory, competition,
and the like,
all the way down to the desire for kingship,
that's the attribute of upliftedness;
that surely the attribute of kingship, of leadership, includes all ten things:
there's desire, *chafetz*, which means like a craving, to be a king,

and there's a whole creative wisdom that you have to have of how you're going to make the laws and how you're going to run your country, and then there's the emotions, and there's thought, speech, and action.

blocks.text: **And the same way with a different character trait within yourself, like the attribute of gevura**, which is, let's say, severity or justice: the thing that you want everything to be fair and just. If a person has a sense of justice, that automatically includes all the details: in every situation, in every circumstance, he will want to do the fair thing, and things should be deserved and worked for. A whole worldview comes along with it.

**And the same thing with beauty, or showing off**: a person with a sense of beauty wants everything to be beautiful, or at least knows how to make everything beautiful, and it comes out in everything; it is a whole worldview too. **And the same thing with winning, with victory, competition**: a person who wants to win, to be the best, very competitive, that desire can come out in everything; he wants to win everything. "It's not like they have a specific desire for each game that they want to win."

**And the like, all the way down to the desire for kingship, that's the attribute of upliftedness**, *hisnasus*: to be over people, higher than them, in charge of them, so that they praise you and are subservient and subordinate.

Surely **the attribute of kingship, of leadership, includes all ten things.** **There's desire, chafetz, which means like a craving, to be a king**, and there is a whole creative wisdom you have to have, of how you are going to make the laws and run your country; and then there are the emotions, and thought, speech and action. "There's a lot goes into being a king." So we must say that a king has all those things.

phrases.he: אך קודם שבא לבחינת התגלות בדבר פרט,
phrases.en: But before the attribute of kingship is revealed in a particular thing,
like to be king of this country,

phrases.he: כלולים ומתאחדים בתכלית בבחינת מדת המלוכה ההיולית העצמית
phrases.en: all these details were included and united completely in the central attribute of kingship within himself,

phrases.he: כמו בעצמות חפץ חסד ההיולי הנ"ל
phrases.en: just like we spoke about the essential power of kindness in yourself.

blocks.title: Napoleon as a baby
blocks.text:
Take a great king and world dictator, like Napoleon. He conquered a lot of the world, the whole of Europe, and started conquering Russia; he wanted to be a world dictator. So he had a big, great desire to be king, and a big intellect of how he would do it and what his laws would be, a whole system and a whole theory of how these countries would run, the French Revolution, everything like that. But all those details are just the way it came out when he actually did it, a particular thing, like a kind person giving a coat. That was the particular way his desire to be king came out.

Really, as soon as he was born he already had in him the desire to be king; the proof is that later he wanted to be king. But the way that attribute of kingship was in him as a baby, he did not yet have the details. He did not know how he would do it; he did not even know what country he was in. He did not know that he wanted to be king of France. "So that's what he's going to say now."
blocks.outOfPlace: He gives the mashal just before he reads line 46, which it illustrates.

blocks.text: **But before the attribute of kingship is revealed in a particular thing, like to be king of this country**, as Napoleon wanted to be king of France and then take over the rest of the world, **all these details were included and united completely in the central attribute of kingship within himself**: in the part of who he is that he is a leader.

Not that he is necessarily actually a leader. Every person has it somewhat, and in some people it is much more prominent: they have leadership ability, they feel that they are a leader, and it could come out in wanting to be in charge of their eighth-grade class yearbook, or in being king of France. The desire to be a leader, to be on top, that other people should recognize your supremacy and praise you and listen to you, comes out, as he says later in the book, even in a little kid who likes to impose himself on animals: "the little kids who go to a dog and press their head down and sit on them." That is a thing of kingship too. But the main thing of kingship is over people who are otherwise your equals.
blocks.title: The yearbook and the dog

blocks.text: **Just like we spoke about the essential power of kindness in yourself**: just as the kindness includes all the shoes and the coats, so the attribute of kingship includes all the different countries. It is not really that the details are there. It is a higher thing, a higher essence, and if you have the essence, all the details automatically come out; you do not need each detail as a separate thing. That is the analogy.

If so, what are each of the powers of the soul really? What is the real thing of kindness? Not a bunch of particular details: just one essence, that you are kind. It is part of your self-identity, and if you have that identity, that you are a kind person, the details will all come out automatically. The same with all the others, justice and beauty and victory and kingship: they are parts of your identity, just who you are, and if that is who you are, you will automatically want to do this and think like that. Every single person has all ten of them, only he brings them out in different ways. That is a person's individual identity, and that is what he says now.

phrases.en: If so, it's understood automatically

phrases.he: שבחינת מדת העצמיות דכח''ב וחג''ת ונהי''ם ההיולים שבעצמיות הנפש,
phrases.en: that all ten of the essential powers, attributes of yourself: your desire and wisdom and understanding and kindness and severity and beauty and victory and glory and *yesod*, which is like the idea of your relationship, and your kingship, your leadership ability,

phrases.he: לא יתכן לומר גם לשון זה שמתאחדים וכלולים בעצמיות הנפש הנקרא יחידה
phrases.en: we can't even say that these are ten different attributes that have distinct identities and that they're just somehow united and included within the essence of your soul, which is called the *yechida*, within your inner self.

blocks.text: **If so, it's understood automatically that all ten of the essential powers, attributes of yourself** (your desire, wisdom, understanding, kindness, severity, beauty, victory, glory, *yesod*, "which is like the idea of your relationship", and your kingship, your leadership ability) are all aspects of who you are. And this is not even just your identity, your self-image: it is actually what you are as a human being, part of the essence of your soul. **We can't even say that these are ten different attributes that have distinct identities and that they're just somehow united and included within the essence of your soul, which is called the yechida.** We cannot say that in your inner self there is one part of you that is kind and another part that is wise, and they are put together and make you. Really, there is just you. You are one simple essence; you are just you.

By just being you, "like how they tell you always, just be yourself", it all comes out. You do not have to try to impress people that you are kind, that you are wise, whatever it is. If you just be yourself, all those things will come out automatically. Just as when a person tries to be kind the shoes and the coats come out by themselves, if you just try to be yourself, the wisdom and the kindness and all those things will come out, because that is just who you are. The essence of each of those attributes is just you: that you are kind, that you are wise. They are not separate things; it is just you.

Further, there is a general thing: there is just you as a human being. There is a certain essence of what a person is, just as there is a certain essence of what kindness is. When that human factor is expressed in the realm of intellect, it comes out as wisdom; when it is expressed in the realm of emotion, it comes out as kindness and justice and the rest, because these are human attributes. "People are kind. Rocks aren't kind. Plants aren't kind." So all those attributes are like shoes and coats: the way the human element is expressed in different arenas. It is really one essence, a human thing.

Every person also has his own individual style and twist on the human element. That is why, if each person just is himself, it will come out in each situation: everyone will know how to act according to who he is. But at the core, every person, by the fact that he is a person, has the potential for all ten of these automatically. It is not a bunch of separate things put together to make him. There is something higher than all of them, which is that he is a person, and when you put that into intellect it comes out as creativity and as logic.

This is like all the sci-fi books and movies where they try to make artificial intelligence, computers and robots, and try to give them all the characteristics. There are certain things you cannot give them; there is something higher than a programmed thing. You need a certain essence, which is like the soul, the human element. For example, humor: "You can't teach a computer humor, and you can't teach creativity to a computer," because these are part of the human element that is higher than all these things. You can make a computer do computations, so it has intellect, but not human intellect; it is missing that essence. So all ten attributes are one essence: the human element, expressed and applied in all different ways.

What he is doing here is showing us the idea of an essence, a *hiyuli*, that kind of relationship: something higher than the details, a higher essence, and when you have that point you automatically have all the details; a singular point. He showed it in the example of kindness, and said the same applies to any other attribute. Then he says there is really a higher essence that unites all ten attributes. Each attribute, relative to what comes out of it, has an essence: kindness is the essence of all the kind deeds, *gevura*, justice, the essence of all the just deeds. Put all ten human attributes together and you find an essence that unites them all: the human essence.
