blocks.text: And if you continue you can go higher. There is a human element, an animal element, a plant element, angels and whatever, all different kinds of things, and if you look you find an essence behind all of them: the G-dly essence. And you can keep going higher and higher, even within G-dliness, to the way G-dliness is revealed within the ten *sefiros*; but the next chapter will explain those ideas.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 14 opens by summing up class 13 (lines 46-48) and the kindness mashal before it, then reads line 49; placed under line 48, which it restates.

blocks.text: That is the basic idea of what he is doing: first he gives an analogy of an essence in a simpler, more concrete example, the relationship of kindness to shoes and coats, and then he says that this shows us how it is with the essence of the soul and all ten attributes, a higher essence. So all ten essential attributes of the essence of the soul are really one. We cannot say they are separate things that unite in the *yechida*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 14 opens by summing up class 13 (lines 46-48) and the kindness mashal before it, then reads line 49; placed under line 48, which it restates.

phrases.he: מאחר שאינן נבדלים מן העצם כלל
phrases.en: because each of these attributes are not separate from the essence at all, from the self at all.

phrases.he: כמו מדת חפץ חסד ההיולי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Like for example, the attribute of kindness,
that it's impressed in his nature and in his self.

blocks.text: Why not? Why can't we say that? **Because each of these attributes are not separate from the essence at all, from the self at all.** You cannot have wisdom without a person, and you cannot have kindness without a person. They are inseparable from the essence behind them, which is the human essence.

**Like for example, the attribute of kindness**: really only people have this thing of kindness, **that it's impressed in his nature and in his self.** It is not a separate thing from him that was put on him; it is impressed into him, a property he has.

blocks.title: Water and a car engine
blocks.text: What it means for something to be impressed in the nature of a thing: water has a lot of properties. It boils at a certain temperature and freezes at a certain temperature, it dissolves things, it is a liquid at room temperature, and when it freezes it expands. You cannot find one part of the water that freezes, a different part that boils and a different part that dissolves things. It is not like a car, where there is the engine that pulls it and there are the wheels, separate things you could take out. You could take the engine out of a car, "and then you would have a car that only works downhill," and use the engine to run something else. With water there is no one part you could take out and leave the rest of the properties without it, because none of them has a physical existence; they are just the nature of the molecule. If you have water, you have all of them. "It's an all-or-nothing deal."

"It's not a perfect analogy", and the Mitteler Rebbe does not give it here. It is not meant as an analogy for what is being said, only as an explanation of what he means by "impressed in the nature and the self."

That is the nature of people, human nature: if there is a person, he has these attributes automatically. All people, just by being people, have a thing of being kind, the potential for kindness. It is not a separate thing that you could take out and still have a person without the kindness. It is all or nothing: if you have a person, he has this thing. If a person does not seem to show any capacity for kindness, they say he is not a person, "he's a monster," because every person has it within him. And really even those people have it; they just do not show it so much.

And a person who looks as if he is only kind, never gets angry: they say he is not human, maybe that he is an angel, "they say whatever," but not like a person. Then when they see him get angry, they say, "Oh, now I see that you're human." This is an inextricable part of human nature: people have a thing of kindness, and also a thing of justice and severity, a sense of justice that is natural to them.

phrases.he: הגם שהוא חלק אחד הנמשך מעצם הנפש ממש, שלמעלה מהיות חפץ חסד בעצמיות,
phrases.en: The idea of kindness is only one detail that comes from the essence of the soul, and really the essence of the soul is higher than being kindness.

phrases.he: שזהו ענין פרטי ממהותה העצמית הפשוטה בתכלית
phrases.en: This is only one little aspect of my real self, which is really simple, completely simple.

phrases.he: מכל מקום אי אפשר לומר בו שמתאחד במדת נצוח ההיולית הנטוע בעצם הנפש,
phrases.en: Nevertheless, you can't say that it's like a separate thing that unites with the attribute of victory, of winning, competitiveness, that's in you,

phrases.he: מאחר שמיוחדים שניהם בעצמות ואינן נבדלים כלל וכלל מן העצם
phrases.en: because they're totally one in yourself, and they're not at all separate from yourself; they're just really you.

blocks.text: **The idea of kindness is only one detail that comes from the essence of the soul, and really the essence of the soul is higher than being kindness.** A person is not defined by kindness: as was just said, you also have to have justice and the other things.

You cannot define the totality of a person as being kindness, and "I can't hold myself back, even though we're not talking about the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for) yet": for sure you cannot define G-d as being kindness, and say that His totality is kindness. To mean that G-d is only kindness and does not have *gevura* "is heresy. That's making G-d more limited even than a person."

So even though the real essence of a person is higher than kindness, you cannot say, "That's who I am: I am kindness, that's it." No, I'm me. It is only one aspect of who I am. **This is only one little aspect of my real self, which is really simple, completely simple**, above these things. I am something higher that transcends kindness, "and I don't have to be nice if I don't want to." That is why you have choice in how to act: you are really higher than any of these things, and you can choose which way to express yourself.

**Nevertheless**, even though kindness is only one aspect of yourself, **you can't say that it's like a separate thing that unites with the attribute of victory, of winning, competitiveness, that's in you**, as if they were two separate things being put together within you, **because they're totally one in yourself, and they're not at all separate from yourself; they're just really you.** There are not two things, kindness and competitiveness, that you put together and get you. There is just you. When you are put into a situation that has a potential for kindness, you bring out yourself in a way of kindness; when you come into a situation that has a potential for competition, the competition comes out. The human essence expresses itself in different areas in different ways, but it is really one simple thing.

sections.title: More meshalim: the cat's power of movement, consciousness, and the sun
sections.summary: The power of movement in a living thing, the soul's consciousness before it spreads into the eye and the ear, and the light in the body of the sun all show the same relation: the essence includes every particular that will come out of it, yet in the essence there is no movement, no seeing, no light at all. We speak of the particulars as united there only from the side of what will come out.

phrases.en: Like for example,
the power of movement,
the way that it's included within the essence of a living thing, within like an animal,
before it moved,
it's not separate from the self at all.

phrases.he: אף על פי שבגלוי כח התנועה להניע דבר פרט, יתחלק לכמה פרטי אופנים,
phrases.en: Even though when it's revealed and it actually moves, then it becomes a bunch of particular movements,

phrases.he: אי אפשר לומר שכל אופני פרטי התנועה כלולים ומתאחדים היו, כשהיה כח התנועה נכלל בעצם החי
phrases.en: we can't say that all of these particular movements existed as separate things and were united in this power of movement the way that it's in the essence of the cat,

phrases.he: מאחר שאז לא היה בסוג וגדר תנועה כלל,
phrases.en: because then, the way that it was included in the essence, it wasn't in the whole realm or category of movement at all,
not in general and not in particular.

blocks.text: That is the end of this analogy. Now come a few more, because this is the main one, but the others help to get a clearer picture. It always helps to have a few analogies: it is impossible to give a perfect analogy, so each one helps fill in where the others are lacking.

blocks.title: The cat that ate its cat food
blocks.text: Take a cat, or a person, or any healthy living being. The cat ate its cat food that day, and it has energy, it has strength, it is able to move. But that potential, the strength it got from its cat food that lets it move, until it moves, is not really something separate from it at all. And as far as the soul of the cat goes, the soul can move its body. But when a cat is sleeping it is not moving; it is just lying there, breathing, basically not moving. You do not see it, but just by being a living thing, it has the ability to move.

blocks.title: The cat stalking a mouse
blocks.text: **Even though when it's revealed and it actually moves, then it becomes a bunch of particular movements.** When the cat goes stalking a mouse, it creeps up quietly behind it, crouches down, pounces and slams its paw down on the mouse, beats it around a little, and then eats it. There is a whole bunch of particular, very calculated movements: the cat is a hunter when it stalks quietly and measures exactly how to pounce.

**We can't say that all of these particular movements existed as separate things and were united in this power of movement the way that it's in the essence of the cat.** You cannot say the cat has a power to lift its right paw and another for its left paw, then a crouching power and a pouncing power. It is just one thing. As far as the soul goes, it is one thing for sure; and even as far as the body goes, it has the energy from the food it ate, but it does not have to eat special food for moving each foot and for jumping and for crouching. It is just this simple energy. It is true that when it comes into the body, the way the muscles and bones are shaped lets it move in certain ways. But the energy is the same energy, and the cat's power to control the body just tells it to move this, to move that.

It is the same signal that tells the right arm to move and the left one; one goes to this one and one goes to that one. The soul tells the brain, the brain sends an electrochemical impulse through the nerves, it tells the muscle to pull, and the muscle pulls; which way you move depends on which muscle you tell to pull. But it is the same thing: a simple ability to control the body, and physically, too, a simple energy from what it ate. That energy is also called the power of movement.

blocks.title: One outlet for the toaster and the radio
blocks.text: It is like electricity. You can plug whatever you want into your outlet; you do not need a special outlet for your toaster and another for your radio. Electricity is this essence of force, and you can plug whatever you want into it. So too the cat gets a certain energy from its food, and then it can move however it wants with it, because it is the essence of energy, the essence of movement, and it includes any movement it wants. And in the soul of the cat there is the spiritual power of movement that controls the body and tells it what to do. Whichever way you look at it, the individual movements are not there as separate things.

**Because then, the way that it was included in the essence, it wasn't in the whole realm or category of movement at all, not in general and not in particular.** Even the general idea of movement was not there, to move this arm or that arm, or even up and down, and for sure not particular movements, "twitching its top left whisker." So even though it includes all the details, you see very clearly that they are not there as individual things: it is just this higher, simple essence, and everything else comes out from it.

phrases.he: וכן בחינת גילוי התפשטות החיות להחיות כל הגוף בעודנו כלול לגמרי בעצם רוח החיים
phrases.en: The same thing with consciousness, the soul's power of consciousness, before it spreads out into the body to give it life, the way that it's just included in the essence of your soul.
So even though when it's revealed,

phrases.he: מתחלק לראיה ושמיעה לעין ואוזן וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: when your consciousness is revealed, it goes into your eye and into your ear and becomes seeing and hearing and the like,

phrases.he: שבודאי גם טרם בואו להתגשם בעין ואוזן בפועל,
phrases.en: surely even before it was revealed, before you actually saw something or actually heard something,

phrases.he: היה כלול בו חיות הראיה הרוחנית לעין בפני עצמו, וחיות השמיעה באוזן בפני עצמו
phrases.en: your soul had the ability to see and to hear.
Nevertheless,

phrases.he: קודם שבאה עצם הנפש לכלל בחינת התפשטות החיות,
phrases.en: before the essence of the soul came to actually go into your body and perceive things, and see, and hear, and feel,
even though these abilities are included in it,

phrases.he: הרי זה כהתכללות כח התנועה בעצם החי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: this is the same way that the power of movement is included in the essence of the cat.

blocks.text: **The same thing with consciousness, the soul's power of consciousness, before it spreads out into the body to give it life**, the way it is just included in the essence of your soul: if you are sitting in a dark, quiet room, you are not seeing anything and not hearing anything. When that power of consciousness is revealed it comes out as seeing and hearing and feeling and tasting and smelling. But the power of consciousness is really the same for hearing and for seeing; it is not really two different powers.

Even physically, in your brain, it is one thing. Your eyes go to your brain and your ears go to the brain, and in the brain they are the same: there is no difference between the signal from the eye and the signal from the ear as it is in the brain. The difference is only which part of the brain it goes to, or the exact order it comes in. As far as what is going on, it is the same impulses flying through your brain, and your brain perceives them as different things. That is the essence of what is really going on.

**So even though when it's revealed, when your consciousness is revealed, it goes into your eye and into your ear and becomes seeing and hearing and the like, surely even before it was revealed, before you actually saw something or actually heard something, your soul had the ability to see and to hear.** You see this very clearly here, because your eye does not really see: your soul sees.

blocks.title: If a tree falls in the forest
blocks.text:
This is a little hard to explain to people at first, but even science talks about it: the difference between physical things and psycho-physical things. Take loudness. Loudness is not a physical thing; it is a human thing, the way you perceive a sound. The physical thing is how much air it moves, called amplitude: the louder something is, the more air it pushes when it vibrates. So when they ask, "If a tree falls in a forest and nobody's there to hear it, does it make a sound?" the answer is no. It moves a lot of air, but the sound only exists in your head; there is no sound from the tree.

The same with seeing: there is no real thing of color in the world. Light hits things and bounces off at different frequencies, the frequencies hit your eye, your eye sends signals to your brain, and your soul sees them as different colors. It is really all coming from your soul.

Since it is all coming from your soul, we must say that hearing and seeing, and the different colors and sounds, were already included in your soul, and that your soul already had within it the potential for seeing and hearing as different things; otherwise, where would the differences come from? They do not really come from your eyes and your ears. Your eyes and ears only trigger it to be revealed. So it is a *hiyuli* again, an essence.

blocks.title: "I can't see that chair"
blocks.text: Once you have the power of seeing, you can see everything. You can never tell a person, "Oh, you see that chair over there?" "What chair?" "You know, the chair right there." "No, I guess I can't see that chair." That is never going to happen, because if you have the power to see, you can see anything. Sometimes there is a problem with a person's eye, he is color blind or this or that, but that is just a physical defect, like putting a blindfold on a person: it does not take away his real power to see; it is just not being revealed.

blocks.title: Out of salt-passing movements
blocks.text: The same with the power of movement. You cannot say, "I'd love to pass you the salt, but I ran out of passing-the-salt movements. I used my last one up for the last guy." You cannot run out of them and you cannot be missing them, because once you have the essence, you have everything.

**Nevertheless, before the essence of the soul came to actually go into your body and perceive things, and see, and hear, and feel, even though these abilities are included in it, this is the same way that the power of movement is included in the essence of the cat**: the particular movements are not there. In the same way, the particular things of seeing and hearing are not in the essence of your soul; they are revealed only afterwards, when it comes into the body. There it is just one simple thing: your soul has the ability to perceive, to be conscious of things.

phrases.he: וכל מה שמוכן ועתיד לבוא לידי גלוי בפועל החיות עדיין,
phrases.en: As long as you're talking about what's going to come out,

phrases.he: יתכן היחוד וההתכללות דראיה ושמיעה וכהאי גוונא
אבל כאשר כלול לגמרי בעצם הנפש
phrases.en: but when we're speaking about the way it was included completely in the self, the essence of the soul,

phrases.he: והיה כלא יש במציאות התפשטות חיות כלל וכלל
phrases.en: if you look at the essence of the soul, the whole idea of consciousness, it's as if it doesn't exist.

phrases.he: מצד עצם הנפש שלמעלה הרבה מבחינת התפשטות,
phrases.en: When you're looking at it from the point of view of the essence of the soul, which is much higher than spreading out to be conscious of things in a body,

phrases.he: רק שכולל בעצמות גם כן בחינת ההתפשטות,
phrases.en: just that the essence also includes this ability to perceive things,

phrases.he: כעצם החי שכולל בעצמו כח התנועה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: just like the essence of a living thing that includes the power of movement.

blocks.text: **As long as you're talking about what's going to come out**, you ask how it will come out. When the soul comes into the body, can it see? Yes, it can see. Can it hear? Yes, it can hear. So there you can say there are different powers, seeing and hearing, because once revealed they are different, and you say the soul has all of them: the soul must have the ability to see and the ability to hear. It sounds as if you are talking about a bunch of different things that the soul puts together, because you are retracing it back. You are saying that when it is revealed they are different, and so all these things we see as different were included there before it came out.

**But when we're speaking about the way it was included completely in the self, the essence of the soul**, not the way it will come into the body but the way it is right now, **if you look at the essence of the soul, the whole idea of consciousness, it's as if it doesn't exist.** There is no idea of perceiving things.

**When you're looking at it from the point of view of the essence of the soul, which is much higher than spreading out to be conscious of things in a body**, you do not see anything there. You say there is no seeing and no hearing, just the soul, no type of consciousness of these things. **Just that the essence also includes this ability to perceive things**: "also", *gam kein*, is the main word. **Just like the essence of a living thing that includes the power of movement.** There are no movements now at all; it is not moving, so you do not see any movements. But it has the ability: if the soul comes into the body, it can move, and even once it is in the body, the energy it ate can come out as movements. There is no existence of a movement right now. In the same way, in the essence of the soul there are no colors or sounds, just the essence of the soul; only when it comes out can you say there are all the different things.

phrases.he: אם כן איך יתכן בחינת היחוד והתכללות דפרטי אור וחיות
phrases.en: If so, when is it fitting to speak about the unity and the inclusion of all the particular lights and consciousness, feelings?

phrases.he: רק מצד שעתיד ומוכן לצאת בהתפשטות חיות בהתחלקות פרטי חיות
phrases.en: Only because you're saying that when it comes into the body, then it's going to be divided into seeing and hearing and all these,
From this we're forced to say,

phrases.he: שיש כל פרטים הללו בהתפשטות הכלולה בעצם לגמרי,
phrases.en: you must say that every single detail that's going to come out was already included in the essence, in the soul.

phrases.he: שאם לא כן מאין נמצאו פרטים הללו
phrases.en: Because if not, where do they come from
when they're revealed?

phrases.he: כמו האור וזיו שכלול בעצם השמש,
phrases.en: Like the light and the ray that was included in the essence of the sun,

phrases.he: שיש בו בהעלם כל פרטי אופני זיו המתפשט וכהאי גוונא ודי למבין.

blocks.text: **If so, when is it fitting to speak about the unity and the inclusion of all the particular lights and consciousness?** **Only because you're saying that when it comes into the body, then it's going to be divided into seeing and hearing and all these**, red and green, all the different sounds and colors and tastes and smells. When you speak about the way it is going to come out, you can say that all those separate things were included and united there.

**From this we're forced to say** that every single detail that is going to come out was already included in the essence, in the soul. **Because if not, where do they come from when they're revealed?** Since they came from the essence, we must say they are there. But we are not saying they exist there as separate things; only that everything that comes out of it must have come from there. So we say it has seeing and it has hearing, but there is no existence of seeing and hearing there yet. They are not separate things, and at that point seeing and hearing are really the same thing. Only when it is revealed in the body, in the physical world, is it revealed as different things, and so we say that all those different things came from there.

blocks.title: The sun and the light bulb filament
blocks.text:
**Like the light and the ray that was included in the essence of the sun.** The sun is a big ball of hydrogen gas undergoing nuclear fusion, and in the actual body of the sun there is no light. What there is, is this stuff, and because it is very hot, "we don't really need to get into all the physics of it," its nature causes light: the electrons get excited and give off photons, "whatever." How it happens does not matter right now.

The actual body of the sun is like a light bulb with its filament, the wire inside that gets hot. The wire has no light in it. It is just a wire whose nature is that when you run electricity through it, it gets hot and glows and gives off light. Even while it is on and glowing, the wire is still not light; if you look inside the wire you do not see light. The light just comes out from it.

blocks.title: Every ray and color is in the sun
blocks.text: In the same way, the sun already has in it the ability to make light: not just general white light, but each ray, each color. If the sun were a little different it would make different colors; it would not make the exact mix of red and blue and yellow that it makes, and it would not look white. It would look red, or blue: different stars have different colors depending on what they are made of. Because of what the sun is made of, it makes this kind of light, with this exact combination of the spectrum. And all the details of its rays, not just the colors but the ultraviolet and the infrared, the heat, the growth of plants, all come from the sun. Nevertheless, the way they are there, there is no light yet at all.

We must say they all come from the sun: the exact light that comes through our window, traced all the way back through outer space, comes from the sun. There is a level where it is in the sun just as we see it, in the bits of space between the pieces of the sun, where there is light too. But in the actual stuff of the sun there is no light yet. So though we say, "Oh, the sun has red, and it has blue, and it has all these things," in the actual body of the sun none of these things are there yet; it can just bring them all out.

In the same way, the essence of the soul has all these things when it comes out, but in the soul itself not only do you not see these details, the whole idea of them does not exist yet, because it is a higher essence, the source of these things. If you have the sun you automatically have the light, because one of the things it can do is bring out light. But the sun is much higher than light; light is not all it is. "It's not like a big ball of light, and it's just leaking it out slowly." It is something that makes light, and it also does other things.

That is the analogies. Whenever analogies are used in *Chassidus* they are very exact. When more than one analogy is used there is a reason, and the analogies are chosen because they actually come from the spiritual thing they are talking about. So it is very important to stick to the analogies of the book; but once you understand the general idea, you can also see it in everything.

blocks.title: Mozart as a little kid
blocks.text: You can see this relationship in a talent, like a talent for music. Take Mozart when he was a little kid. He did not have all the particular songs; why couldn't he just write them all out? Because in his talent the particular songs are not there yet. And yet only he is going to come up with these songs: they come out from his style and his talent, and it is just a matter of bringing it out. The same with all kinds of things like that. But these are the main analogies, the ones given here.

*V'dai l'mevin* ("and this is enough for one who understands"). As was said before, whenever it says *v'dai l'mevin*, it means that you will understand the idea if you know how to understand the analogies: to know which part applies and which part does not, and to throw out the parts of the metaphor that do not apply. That is the way it is with any metaphor; you need a certain common sense to know what the person is talking about.

blocks.title: An eagle in the sky
blocks.text: If they are talking about a warplane flying and they say, "It was an eagle in the sky," what do you mean it was an eagle? It was a plane. That is how metaphors work: the whole idea of a metaphor is that you are saying it is something it is not. The same here: all these analogies are not at all what we are talking about, and most of the limitations that apply to them, none of them, apply to what we are talking about. There are a few points, maybe two or three, that we are trying to bring out, and everything else you have to forget about.

That is the idea that you should not be *magshim* (make physical) the idea. When you give a *mashal*, the *mashal* is supposed to be a very physical, simple one, specifically, and you are supposed to understand the analogies literally. Some people think that since you are not supposed to be *magshim* *Chassidus*, you should not understand the *meshalim* as simple physical *meshalim*. But the Rebbe says that you are supposed to understand them as simple physical *meshalim*: that is the *mashal*. The more simply and physically you understand the *mashal*, the better: you should want to see it in your daily life as a real thing you know in the world. The *nimshal*, though, is not like the *mashal*; that is what not being *magshim* means. You should not think it is *mamash* like this at all. So in the next chapter a lot of the limitations that apply to the analogies will have to be taken away. "Eat the fruit and throw out the peel." As it says, Rabbi Meir came and found a pomegranate, and he ate the fruit and threw out the peel.

sections.title: Three levels in the soul: Yachid, Echad and Kadmon
sections.summary: From the *yechida* come three levels, one after the other. First, the ten essential *hiyuli* powers, included in the self as movement is in a living thing: no separate things at all (*Yachid*). Second, the powers ready to come to a particular thing, where many details are united in one general point (*Echad*). Third, everything estimated and prepared in detail, lacking only the deed (*Kadmon*).

phrases.en: So it comes out

phrases.he: ג' מדריגות זה אחר זה נמשך מעצמיות הנפש ממש, הנקרא בחינת יחידה
phrases.en: that there are three levels, one after the other, that come from the essence of the soul, which is called *yechida*.

blocks.text: **So it comes out that there are three levels, one after the other, that come from the essence of the soul, which is called yechida.** The original analogy, brought to explain these three steps of *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, was the way the powers of the soul are revealed from the *yechida*. So we see that in the revelation from the *yechida* there are three corresponding steps.

phrases.en: The first step:
are the ten essential and *hiyuli* powers, the self and essential powers,
like the essential desire and kindness in the self,
and the like with any other thing, with desire for *gevura*, or desire for *netzach*, or anything else,
just like the way the power of movement is in the essence of the living thing,

phrases.he: וכהתכללות התפשטות החיות בעצם כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: in the same way, with the inclusion of consciousness in the self.

blocks.text: **The first step are the ten essential and hiyuli powers, the self and essential powers, like the essential desire and kindness in the self, and the like with any other thing, with desire for gevura, or desire for netzach, or anything else.**

They are included in it completely. Part of who a person is, is that he has this thing of kindness; included in who he is, is that he has this thing of *gevura*, of severity and judgement, and the thing of *netzach*, to win. As was said before, these are part of him, of who he is. **Just like the way the power of movement is in the essence of the living thing**, the cat: there it is not a movement at all, only that by the nature of what it is, it also has the power of movement, but there is no actual movement there yet. **In the same way, with the inclusion of consciousness in the self**: there is no actual perception of sights or sounds there yet, just the soul, which by the nature of what it is automatically has the power of consciousness. But it totally does not exist now as a separate entity.

phrases.he: ולא יתכן בהם לומר לשון התאחדות מדברים נבדלים יחד
phrases.en: You can't say that there's like these separate things that are put together there,
because they're totally included in the self; it's really just the self.

phrases.he: והיה כלא היה במציאות כלל וכלל כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: It's as if they don't exist at all, because only the self exists at this point.

blocks.text: At this stage, speaking of the person himself, of the essence of the human soul, you cannot say that *chesed* and *gevura* are two separate things. It is just the person, just the fact that he is human. When he comes out into the world, this humanness is sometimes expressed as kindness and sometimes as severity, but they are not separate things there. At that stage in the soul the whole idea of kindness and severity does not exist yet; it is just a simple humanness. The same with the power of movement: you cannot say different movements are included there, because there is no thing of movements there yet, just life; there is no existence of movement yet. The same with perceptions: there are no sights, no sounds, no colors, no pitch, just the soul. So **you can't say that there's like these separate things that are put together there**, because they do not exist yet.

**Because they're totally included in the self; it's really just the self. It's as if they don't exist at all, because only the self exists at this point.** All that is included in its existence is that it can give rise to these existences. By the nature of what it is these things exist there, but not as distinct, separate entities. Those distinctions do not exist yet; the things are derived from the essence, from the self, but to the self they are really all the same thing.

phrases.en: In the second stage

phrases.he: בחינת התפשטות י' כחות שמוכנים לבא בבחינת גלוי
phrases.en: is the extension of the ten powers of the soul when they're ready to be revealed,

phrases.he: כמו חפץ חסד העצמי ההיולי שבא לדבר חסד בדרך פרט
phrases.en: like, for example, when a person's inner desire for kindness comes to a particular thing,
even before he did it, so he didn't actually give the person the thing yet,

phrases.he: רק כשעתיד ומוכן לצאת לדבר פרט
phrases.en: just that it's ready to come to this particular thing.
At this point

phrases.he: יתכן ענין האחדות מכמה פרטים שבו
כמו שכל ומדות שבחפץ חסד זה
phrases.en: like the intellect and emotions in this desire for kindness,
when the *chesed* comes out from the hiddenness of the *hiyuli*.

blocks.text: **In the second stage is the extension of the ten powers of the soul when they're ready to be revealed, like, for example, when a person's inner desire for kindness comes to a particular thing**: he wants to get somebody a present for his birthday, or to give the person the coat or the shoes.

blocks.title: The coat at the door, before the details
blocks.text: **Even before he did it, so he didn't actually give the person the thing yet, just that it's ready to come to this particular thing.** With the poor man and the coat: he opens the door, sees a poor man and wants to help him. Automatically he already knows that he wants to give him a coat, but he has not figured out exactly which coat, where it is, where he will get it, whether he will buy him one or give him one of his old coats. He has not figured out the details; he knows the general thing, that he wants to give him a coat. Before he opened the door, sitting in his chair, he just had the thing that he is a nice guy, part of who he is. Now he already wants to do a particular thing based on his kindness: he wants to give him a coat.

**At this point** you can say that he has a general desire to give him a coat, and that desire already recognizes that there will be many details, but they are all included in one general point: he wants to give him a coat. He does not yet see the details as distinct things, because they are all coming together; but the details already *mamash* exist there.

**Like the intellect and emotions in this desire for kindness.** At this point there already is the idea of the intellect and the emotions. Once the desire comes out, included in that point is the way the *sechel* is going to be and the way the *middos* are going to be. It is already all revealed there; it only needs to be brought out in actuality into each of the details. He already has the general thing, that he will have to come up with a *sechel* that evaluates the best way to give him the coat and what coat would be best for this guy. He recognizes that. He recognizes that certain emotions will be involved. But he sees them all as one general thing, how they will work together.

blocks.title: The right-size coat
blocks.text: The final product, when it is all put together, is that he gave him a coat that is appropriate, and it can be a kindness. The kindness is made up of a lot of different acts and parts, and *davka* (precisely) when they are all put together, it is the real kindness. If he did not use his *sechel* and did not give the guy the right-size coat, it would not really be a kindness, "especially if it's too small." So he recognizes that there are going to be all these details, and *davka* when they are put together, that is the kindness.

So at that stage you can say there are actually different levels, all coming together once it comes to relate to a particular thing. **When the chesed comes out from the hiddenness of the hiyuli**, you can already say there are the details, but they are all included. That is the level of *Echad*.

phrases.en: In the third stage,
when it comes to actually do this particular thing,

phrases.he: רק שעדיין לא בא מצד העדר ומניעה
phrases.en: but it just didn't happen yet because something is holding him back;
but from his part he's totally ready to do it,

phrases.he: ולא חסר רק לבא בהתגלות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: he just didn't actually do it yet.

phrases.he: דהיינו שכבר שיער היטב בעצמו בדרך פרט לאותו דבר שבא לפועל ממש
phrases.en: That means that he already estimated very well in himself, in a detailed way, for that thing, how it's going to come in actuality.

phrases.he: והיינו שיער בעצמו בכח מה שצריך להביא בפועל
phrases.en: And this means that he estimates in himself, in potential, what he's going to need to do in actuality.

blocks.text: **In the third stage, when it comes to actually do this particular thing**, it is ready to come out and actually do it, **but it just didn't happen yet because something is holding him back.** **But from his part he's totally ready to do it**: he is totally prepared and has figured out exactly what he is going to do and everything; **he just didn't actually do it yet**, because something is holding him up.

blocks.title: Locked out with the coat
blocks.text: He has figured it all out: he has the perfect coat, and he knows exactly what he is going to do: give that coat to this guy. That is all figured out. And then the wind comes and blows the door shut, and he gets locked out outside with the guy. So he cannot do it yet; he has to ring the doorbell and wait for somebody to let him in, and then he can give him the coat. But he was all ready to do it, he knows exactly what he is going to do, and it is all prepared.

**That means that he already estimated very well in himself, in a detailed way, for that thing, how it's going to come in actuality. And this means that he estimates in himself, in potential, what he's going to need to do in actuality.** That is the level of *Kadmon*.

sections.title: The three levels in movement, consciousness and growth, and the tzimtzum before the deed
sections.summary: The same three stages are in the power of movement, in consciousness and in the power of growth, all before anything actually happens. To pass from spiritual to physical there must first be a *tzimtzum* that narrows the power to one particular way: a decision, a sound or light hitting the senses, a seed in the ground. That is chapter 12.

phrases.he: כמו על דרך דוגמא הנזכר לעיל בכח התנועה
phrases.en: Like in the analogy of the power of movement,
when the power of movement is ready to come out to a particular thing,

phrases.he: וכמו התפשטות החיות להחיות לגוף כשמוכן לצאת
phrases.en: and the same thing with the power of consciousness, that it's going to come out,

phrases.he: שכלולים שם ביחוד כללי כל החיות פרטיי'
phrases.en: that at that stage, all the details are included in one, in a general thing.

blocks.text: **Like in the analogy of the power of movement**, when it is ready to come out to a particular thing, and the same with the spreading of life into the body when it is ready to come out: now he goes back and contrasts the second and third stages in the other two analogies, the power of movement and the power of consciousness. **When the power of movement is ready to come out to a particular thing**, you are going to reach for the salt, or you are playing basketball and going to throw the ball into the hoop: you already know what movement you want to make. **And the same thing with the power of consciousness, that it's going to come out** to *mamash* be a consciousness: it already went from your soul into your brain to be a general consciousness, and now it is ready to go out to your eye and become a thing of seeing.

blocks.title: Reaching for the salt
blocks.text: **At that stage, all the details are included in one, in a general thing.** Once the power of movement comes into your body in general, there is this general physical power, and there you already have all the detailed movements. When a person is going to reach for the salt, he already knows he will have to move his arm like this and like that, the whole process. But you do not think of each detailed movement you have to make, closing your fingers and extending your arm. You just think that you want the salt, as a general movement, and automatically you know that you will make all the particular little movements.

blocks.title: The basketball shot
blocks.text: It is like that with anything, like basketball. You do not think, "Oh, I need to twist my wrist that way and my finger that way." When you are practicing, you do. If you do not have a good shot, then in practice they teach you the technique: hold the ball like this and your finger like that, twist it like that, give it a flick, bend your knees; they tell you all the details. But once you have learned the movement, you just think of the general thing you want, to get the ball in the hoop, and you automatically do all the details without thinking about them. It is actually better not to think about the details: you do a better job if you focus on the general goal, "also because it's distracting."

phrases.en: And after that,

phrases.he: הוא מה ששיער והכין כבר בכח התנועה איך להניע דרך פרט
phrases.en: you have to have that estimation and prepare exactly how you're going to move.

phrases.he: וכן מה ששיער התגלות התפשטות רוח החיים, והוכן בו מה שעתיד להחיות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: In the same way with the power of consciousness, it has to become estimated exactly how it's going to come out.
And similarly, the power of growth of a plant,
when it's ready to grow in actuality,

phrases.he: שיש בזה גם כן ענין ג' מדריגות הללו
phrases.en: that there also, you see these three stages also in the power of growth.

blocks.title: Why one shot goes in
blocks.text: **And after that, you have to have that estimation and prepare exactly how you're going to move.** That is why two people can both know they want to throw the ball into the hoop, and one gets it in and the other does not. One knows how to estimate it properly because he practiced, so he already has the preparation of how to do it, and the other did not practice. You have to have that *shiur* (estimation), that *hashara*, in your power of movement first, of exactly how to do it.

**In the same way with the power of consciousness, it has to become estimated exactly how it's going to come out.** When the power of consciousness goes from your brain to your eye, even before you see something, it now becomes ready to see, and it will not hear from your eye; when it goes into your ear, it becomes ready to hear. So there is already a certain estimation of what kind of thing it is going to perceive: it is ready now to perceive only a sight, or only a sound. That is already a potential estimation of how it is going to come out.

**And similarly**, the Mitteler Rebbe now introduces a new *mashal* he did not bring before, **the power of growth of a plant**: **when it's ready to grow in actuality**, there too you see these three stages.

phrases.he: והכל הוא טרם שבא הדבר עדיין בפועל ממש
phrases.en: But this is all before it actually happens.

blocks.title: The power of growth in the ground
blocks.text: **But this is all before it actually happens.** What are the three stages in the power of growth? First, the power of growth is a spiritual thing, higher than growing any particular plant. Then there is the general power of growth as it comes into the dirt. Really it can grow pretty much anything, and really the dirt is higher than the thing of growth: it is just dirt, only it also has this thing that it can grow. But now it is coming in a limited way: there is a certain general thing there, that it is going to grow something, and it grows only in a certain way; depending on the kind of ground, it is even better for growing certain things than others. And then there is when it is ready to grow a particular thing, a certain tree: you are going to grow an apple tree, and now it is ready to grow that exact tree, but it has not grown it yet.

"I think that the reason that he brings this analogy in is because here you see the need for the *tzimtzum*," which he will explain in the next *inyan*, in chapter 12. In the power of growth you need the seed. If you do not put a seed in the ground, then even though the ground has the potential to grow any tree, and the potential to grow this exact tree, nothing is going to grow. But this is all before it actually happens.

phrases.he: כמו התנועה קודם שבאה בגשם הנפעל
phrases.en: Like the power of movement before it actually comes into the physical thing that is moved,

phrases.he: או החיות הרוחני קודם שבא בגשם הגוף
phrases.en: or the spiritual power of consciousness before it comes into the actual body to actually perceive,

phrases.he: ששם משתנה ממהות רוחנית למהות גשם,
phrases.en: that there, when it goes into the body or the physical thing, it changes from a spiritual thing to a physical thing.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת תנועה גשמיות והחיות גשמיות
phrases.en: Then it becomes a physical movement, that your hand moves and you throw the ball, or a physical consciousness.
And the same way with the actual physical growth of the plant.

phrases.he: שצריך לזה בחינת צמצום וכיווץ בגלוי זה הרוחני בתחלה,
phrases.en: You need something, some sort of a channeling and a contracting to focus this spiritual power so that it should be revealed *davka* in this way,
so that it should go from spiritual to physical,
like he'll explain in chapter 12.

blocks.text: **Like the power of movement before it actually comes into the physical thing that is moved**: you did not actually move anything yet. **Or the spiritual power of consciousness before it comes into the actual body to actually perceive**, before there is the biological, neurochemical signal.

**There, when it goes into the body or the physical thing, it changes from a spiritual thing to a physical thing. Then it becomes a physical movement, that your hand moves and you throw the ball, or a physical consciousness**: the light hits your eye and makes a chemical reaction in your cones and your rods, which sends a signal up the optic nerve to your brain. It is a biological thing. **And the same way with the actual physical growth of the plant**: when the plant actually grows, it changes from a potential for growth to an actual plant.

Before it can come out from the spiritual to the physical, **you need something, some sort of a channeling and a contracting to focus this spiritual power so that it should be revealed davka in this way, so that it should go from spiritual to physical, like he'll explain in chapter 12.**

blocks.title: A decision kills the other options
blocks.text: You see it in the power of growth: you need the seed. And the same in the power of movement. When you actually want to do it, first you just decide in theory that you want to do it and start thinking about how; but then there is a new thing, that you have to decide you actually want to do it. At that point you limit it: you pick which movement you are going to make. "In English the word decision means literally, like, to kill": you kill off all the other options and narrow it down to one. Then you decide you are going to do that, and you actually do it.

The same with the power of seeing and hearing. Even once it has come into your brain and your eye and is ready to see, you are not going to actually see something until light hits your eye, or actually hear something until a sound hits your ear. That is like the seed that focuses it and limits it to come out in one particular way. The difference is that in the *mashal* of the *chesed* and the *mashal* of the power of movement, the *tzimtzum* comes only from you: you decide how to do it. In the *mashal* of the power of perception, of consciousness, and in the power of growth, you clearly see a seed or something that triggers it, so it is easier to see the need for the *tzimtzum* there to bring it out.

reviewQuestions.question: Why must a person contemplate the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* before learning the details of the *hishtalshelus*, and why is studying it "in detail" a paradox?
What is the difference between *Yachid* and *Echad*, and what do the car, the computer and the pure olive oil show about it?
If the *sefiros* there are "not a knowable wisdom", why are they still divisions, and in what sense do we nevertheless say that they are in the Essence?
What does the man on the park bench mean when he says that the kind man's kindness "isn't for anything"?
Why can the ten essential attributes not be called ten things united in the *yechida*?
What are the three levels that come from the *yechida*, and how does the coat at the door show each of them?

notes.text: Mikdash Melech: he says it was written by one of the Arizal's students, "Rabbi Yisrael Saruk, I think was his name", from the Arizal's classes (10 w194-260). The block keeps his words. The printed Mikdash Melech is by Rabbi Shalom Buzaglo (18th century), a commentary on the Zohar that draws on Lurianic teaching in Rabbi Yisrael Saruk's line; a reviewer may want to check what he meant. A garbled phrase there ("he was one of the Arizal's farbrengens", 10 w213-222) is left out of the block.

"In English the word decision means literally like to kill" (17 w2811-2864): kept as he said it. The Latin decidere is de + caedere, "to cut" or "to kill" (as in homicide): to cut off. His gloss is loose, not simply wrong.

Phrases he reads without translating keep their Hebrew alone: the end of line 7 ("hanizkar l'eil"), the second half of line 15, line 26, "v'cha'hai gavna" in line 46, the second half of line 60, the end of line 66, the start of line 69, and the second half of line 75 (at 17 w600-645 he gives a mashal of it, not a rendering). The end of line 22 cites his gloss a few sentences after the reading ("yichud is like unite", 09 w445-454), and most of line 42 cites the sentence right after his reading of it (12 w802-857).

Line 70 is read (17 w0-9) and first rendered loosely (17 w10-47, "you cannot say that... chesed and gevura are two separate things"); its phrase cites his summing-up a little later (17 w185-199), "you can't say that there's like these separate things that are put together there", which is closer to the words. Line 40's two phrases cite the sentence right after he reads it (11 w1400-1453), his translation of the line.

Line 17: the transcript has him say "only that we say that they are wise" (08 w2233-2246), plural, where the text says chakim (He is wise); kept as transcribed. Line 66: he reads "kol pratei pe'ulos hazziv v'hispashtus" (16 w~860), where the chapter has "kol pratei ofanei ziv hamispashet"; possibly the machine's hearing.
Nine of the eleven tapes have Sofer's word times, not re-timed ones (only 15 and 17 are re-timed): the seconds can be off. The word ranges are right.
The Napoleon mashal (13 w0-251) is told just before he reads line 46 and illustrates it; it is placed under lines 46-47 with outOfPlace.

Not flagged: "to mean that G-d is only kindness and does not have gevura is heresy" (14 w1233-1256) is a Torah position stated as such and names no group. Flagged: the remark on charitable foundations (11 w1543-1779).
